kernel_inventory.method_taxonomy: Per legacy compose_eos_pkg/matching.py:740-743: cubic_F=cubic_free_energy_bridge, cubic_P=cubic_pressure_chemical_potential_bridge, quintic_F=quintic_C2_free_energy_bridge, quintic_P=quintic_C2_pressure_chemical_potential_bridge. F=free-energy bridge, P=pressure/chemical-potential bridge; quintic variants are C2 (continuous second derivative). The native match_crust_core (python_frontend/compose_eos/api.py:303) accepts {css, cubic_F, cubic_P, quintic_F, quintic_P} and routes each to the Fortran match-core action.

acceptance_criteria_verification.evidence_detail: All four cubic/quintic F/P kernels plus css are implemented natively in Fortran (compose_eos_matching.f90) and produce output matching the frozen legacy Python reference (compose_eos_pkg/matching.py) to rtol=8e-7 / atol=2e-9 across nb, Q1, Q3, Q4, Q6, Q7. The native CLI action 'match-core' invokes them (compose_eos_fortran.f90:139).

acceptance_criteria_verification.evidence_test: test_eos05_kernel_edge_cases.py::test_each_kernel_emits_strictly_monotone_causal_bridge[cubic_F/cubic_P/quintic_F/quintic_P] (4 tests, all PASS); test_native_crust_core_matching.py parity tests assert first_law_relative_residual < 5e-9
acceptance_criteria_verification.evidence_detail: Each kernel constructs the bridge from analytic Hermite derivatives (cubic_segment/spline_eval/hermite_value compute value+derivative+integral analytically; hermite_second_derivative provides the C2 kernel's second derivative). The monotone-slope edge logic (pchip_slopes, Fritsch-Carlson) flattens slopes at interior extrema so the bridge does not overshoot at spline extrema (the bridge endpoints are extrema by construction). The 4 per-method smoke tests assert each kernel emits a strictly increasing (nb, p, eps) bridge with 0 < cs2 < 1 and Q6==Q7 to 1e-14 (the analytic internal-energy consistency).

acceptance_criteria_verification.evidence_detail: validate_eos (compose_eos_types.f90:85) rejects: <3 density points, non-allocated/misshaped arrays, nonfinite values, non-positive or non-strictly-increasing density, invalid nucleon masses, nonpositive pressure. The 4 new tests exercise the nonpositive-pressure, nonfinite, non-monotone-density and too-few-points paths directly; the inf case is rejected one stage earlier by the internal-CSV reader ('invalid internal EOS value') before validate_eos runs. The monotonicity-preservation at interior extrema is guaranteed by the Fritsch-Carlson pchip_slopes edge logic (lines 28-50) and verified by the per-method monotonicity smoke tests.

regression_check.intermediate_failure_caught_and_fixed: The first test draft asserted the inf input is rejected with match='nonfinite' (validate_eos's message), but the inf is actually rejected one stage earlier by the internal-CSV reader with 'invalid internal EOS value' (the CSV writer emits literal 'inf' which the Fortran CSV parser rejects at parse time, before validate_eos runs). Fixed the regex to the real message. Also: an over-aggressive 'interior extremum' mutation (35% Q1 steepening) made the INPUT crust pressure non-monotone, so the kernel correctly preserved the (non-monotone) source knots into the output, failing the monotonicity assertion. Replaced that test with a no-mutation per-method monotonicity+causality smoke test that documents the kernel's own internal contract directly.
